Leaving a\nward and returning to it later in the shift makes two assignments.\n\n2.4 A transfer from another site immediately before a shift is part of that shift and counts as\none ward assignment.\n\n3 Maximum shift length\n\n3.1 The maximum shift is read from Appendix A by the start time in UK local time and the number\nof ward assignments.\n\n3.2 A shift longer than the Appendix A maximum is an exceedance unless the site manager\nextended it under section 4.\n\n4 Shift extension\n\n4.1 The bleep-holding site manager may extend a shift by up to 01:30 beyond the Appendix A\nmaximum.\n\n4.2 An extension stands only if the shift extension authorisation for that shift is filed and\nsigned by the site manager. An extension without a filed, signed authorisation is treated as no\nextension.\n\n4.3 A shift longer than the Appendix A maximum plus the extension allowed by 4.1 is an\nextension exceedance, measured against that extended limit.\n\n5 Rest\n\n5.1 The minimum rest before a shift is the length of the preceding duty period, and not less\nthan 11:00.\n\n5.2 Rest runs from the end of the preceding duty period to the start of the next shift. On-call\nfrom home does not end a rest period.\n5.3 After a shift that the site manager extended under section 4, the minimum rest that follows\nis increased by the length of the extension.\n\n6 Rolling hours\n\n6.1 Duty periods may not total more than 60:00 in any 7 consecutive days, 110:00 in any 14\n\fconsecutive days or 190:00 in any 28 consecutive days.\n\n6.2 Days are calendar days in UK local time, and each duty period counts in full on the day it\nstarts.\n\n7 On-call\n\n7.1 On-call served on site counts in full as duty. On-call from home counts as one quarter of\nits length.\n\n7.2 A nurse called in from on-call at home starts the shift at the time they report, including\nany transfer; the on-call before the call-in still counts as one quarter.\n\n8 Records\n\n8.1 The ward timesheet is the record of clock-in and clock-out times and of the ward\nassignments worked. Supersedes Revision 6 from that instant.\\n\\n## 1 Which revision applies\\n\\n1.1 A revision applies to every shift whose start time, expressed in UK local time, falls on or after the revision's effective instant. The workforce records hold times in UTC.\\n\\n## 2 Definitions\\n\\n2.1 A shift runs from the time a nurse starts, including any transfer from another site that precedes ward work, to the clock-out time at the end of the last ward assignment worked.\\n\\n2.2 A duty period is a shift plus 30 minutes of handover, or an on-call period.\\n\\n2.3 A ward assignment is one continuous spell on one ward from clock-in to clock-out. Leaving a ward and returning to it later in the shift makes two assignments.\\n\\n2.4 A transfer from another site immediately before a shift is part of that shift and counts as one ward assignment.\\n\\n## 3 Maximum shift length\\n\\n3.1 The maximum shift is read from Appendix A by the start time in UK local time and the number of ward assignments.\\n\\n3.2 A shift longer than the Appendix A maximum is an exceedance unless the site manager extended it under section 4.\\n\\n## 4 Shift extension\\n\\n4.1 The bleep-holding site manager may extend a shift by up to 01:30 beyond the Appendix A maximum.\\n\\n4.2 An extension stands only if the shift extension authorisation for that shift is filed and signed by the site manager. An extension without a filed, signed authorisation is treated as no extension.\\n\\n4.3 A shift longer than the Appendix A maximum plus the extension allowed by 4.1 is an extension exceedance, measured against that extended limit.\\n\\n## 5 Rest\\n\\n5.1 The minimum rest before a shift is the length of the preceding duty period, and not less than 11:00.\\n\\n5.2 Rest runs from the end of the preceding duty period to the start of the next shift. On-call from home does not end a rest period.\\n5.3 After a shift that the site manager extended under section 4, the minimum rest that follows is increased by the length of the extension.\\n\\n## 6 Rolling hours\\n\\n6.1 Duty periods may not total more than 60:00 in any 7 consecutive days, 110:00 in any 14 consecutive days or 190:00 in any 28 consecutive days.\\n\\n6.2 Days are calendar days in UK local time, and each duty period counts in full on the day it starts.\\n\\n## 7 On-call\\n\\n7.1 On-call served on site counts in full as duty. On-call from home counts as one quarter of its length.\\n\\n7.2 A nurse called in from on-call at home starts the shift at the time they report, including any transfer; the on-call before the call-in still counts as one quarter.\\n\\n## 8 Records\\n\\n8.1 The ward timesheet is the record of clock-in and clock-out times and of the ward assignments worked. The shift-actuals record is a transcription and yields to the ward timesheet.\\n\\n8.2 Shift extension authorisations are the record of extensions. The authorisation is the scanned form the extension-authorisations register points to; an extension stands only on an authorisation the site manager has signed, and an authorisation is read as it stands in the register when the audit is closed. The extension flag in the shift-actuals record is a transcription.\\n\\n8.3 The site manager's bleep-log voice notes are the record of call-ins, transfers and where an on-call was served.\\n\\n## Appendix A: maximum shift (hh:mm)\\n\\n| Shift start (UK local) | 1-2 ward assignments | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 or more |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| 06:00 to 13:29 | 13:00 | 12:30 | 12:00 | 11:30 | 11:00 |\\n| 13:30 to 13:59 | 12:45 | 12:15 | 11:45 | 11:15 | 10:45 |\\n| 14:00 to 17:29 | 12:00 | 11:30 | 11:00 | 10:30 | 10:00 |\\n| 17:30 to 04:59 | 11:00 | 10:30 | 10:00 | 09:30 | 09:00 |\\n| 05:00 to 05:59 | 11:30 | 11:00 | 10:30 | 10:00 | 09:30 |\\n\\n\"}}"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c04d0ee3-1507-4573-94d0-03920898b379","uuid":"db1d0817-0c80-4c9d-9386-21c570af2ba9","timestamp":"2026-11-19T05:46:08.153Z","tool_use_result":{"content":"{\"status\":\"ok\",\"output\":{\"file_id\":\"file-ss4-rev7\",\"name\":\"SS-4 Safe Staffing Standard Revision 7.md\",\"mime_type\":\"text/markdown\",\"size_bytes\":4082,\"content\":\"# Marrowgate Health Trust Safe Staffing Standard SS-4: Nurse Shift, Rest and Hours Limits\\n\\nRevision 7. In force from 00:00 UK local time on 15 October 2026. Supersedes Revision 6 from that instant.\n\n## 1 Which revision applies\n\n1.1 A revision applies to every shift whose start time, expressed in UK local time, falls on or after the revision's effective instant. The roster day printed on a roster line does not decide the revision; nor does the date in Coordinated Universal Time.\n\n1.2 UK local time is British Summer Time (UTC plus one hour) until 01:00 UTC on 25 October 2026, when the clocks go back, and Greenwich Mean Time (UTC) after it. The workforce records hold times in UTC.\n\n## 2 Definitions\n\n2.1 A shift runs from the time a nurse starts, including any transfer from another site that precedes ward work, to the clock-out time at the end of the last ward assignment worked.\n\n2.2 A duty period is a shift plus 30 minutes of handover, or an on-call period.\n\n2.3 A ward assignment is one continuous spell on one ward from clock-in to clock-out. Leaving a ward and returning to it later in the shift makes two assignments.\n\n2.4 A transfer from another site immediately before a shift is part of that shift and counts as one ward assignment.\n\n## 3 Maximum shift length\n\n3.1 The maximum shift is read from Appendix A by the start time in UK local time and the number of ward assignments.\n\n3.2 A shift longer than the Appendix A maximum is an exceedance unless the site manager extended it under section 4.\n\n## 4 Shift extension\n\n4.1 The bleep-holding site manager may extend a shift by up to 01:30 beyond the Appendix A maximum.\n\n4.2 An extension stands only if the shift extension authorisation for that shift is filed and signed by the site manager. An extension without a filed, signed authorisation is treated as no extension.\n\n4.3 A shift longer than the Appendix A maximum plus the extension allowed by 4.1 is an extension exceedance, measured against that extended limit.\n\n## 5 Rest\n\n5.1 The minimum rest before a shift is the length of the preceding duty period, and not less than 11:00.\n\n5.2 Rest runs from the end of the preceding duty period to the start of the next shift. On-call from home does not end a rest period.\n5.3 After a shift that the site manager extended under section 4, the minimum rest that follows is increased by the length of the extension.\n\n## 6 Rolling hours\n\n6.1 Duty periods may not total more than 60:00 in any 7 consecutive days, 110:00 in any 14 consecutive days or 190:00 in any 28 consecutive days.\n\n6.2 Days are calendar days in UK local time, and each duty period counts in full on the day it starts.\n\n## 7 On-call\n\n7.1 On-call served on site counts in full as duty. On-call from home counts as one quarter of its length.\n\n7.2 A nurse called in from on-call at home starts the shift at the time they report, including any transfer; the on-call before the call-in still counts as one quarter.\n\n## 8 Records\n\n8.1 The ward timesheet is the record of clock-in and clock-out times and of the ward assignments worked. The shift-actuals record is a transcription and yields to the ward timesheet.\n\n8.2 Shift extension authorisations are the record of extensions. The authorisation is the scanned form the extension-authorisations register points to; an extension stands only on an authorisation the site manager has signed, and an authorisation is read as it stands in the register when the audit is closed. The extension flag in the shift-actuals record is a transcription.\n\n8.3 The site manager's bleep-log voice notes are the record of call-ins, transfers and where an on-call was served.\n\n## Appendix A: maximum shift (hh:mm)\n\n| Shift start (UK local) | 1-2 ward assignments | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 or more |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| 06:00 to 13:29 | 13:00 | 12:30 | 12:00 | 11:30 | 11:00 |\n| 13:30 to 13:59 | 12:45 | 12:15 | 11:45 | 11:15 | 10:45 |\n| 14:00 to 17:29 | 12:00 | 11:30 | 11:00 | 10:30 | 10:00 |\n| 17:30 to 04:59 | 11:00 | 10:30 | 10:00 | 09:30 | 09:00 |\n| 05:00 to 05:59 | 11:30 | 11:00 | 10:30 | 10:00 | 09:30 |\n\n"}}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01RyN9eqa1mp24urhjvTxJdT","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

Retained for shifts that started before that instant.\n\n## 1 Which revision applies\n\n1.1 A revision applies to every shift whose start time, expressed in UK local time, falls on or after the revision's effective instant. The roster day printed on a roster line does not decide the revision; nor does the date in Coordinated Universal Time.\n\n1.2 UK local time is British Summer Time (UTC plus one hour) until 01:00 UTC on 25 October 2026, when the clocks go back, and Greenwich Mean Time (UTC) after it. The workforce records hold times in UTC.\n\n## 2 Definitions\n\n2.1 A shift runs from the time a nurse starts, including any transfer from another site that precedes ward work, to the clock-out time at the end of the last ward assignment worked.\n\n2.2 A duty period is a shift plus 30 minutes of handover, or an on-call period.\n\n2.3 A ward assignment is one continuous spell on one ward from clock-in to clock-out. Leaving a ward and returning to it later in the shift makes two assignments.\n\n2.4 A transfer from another site immediately before a shift is part of that shift. It does not count as a ward assignment.\n\n## 3 Maximum shift length\n\n3.1 The maximum shift is read from Appendix A by the start time in UK local time and the number of ward assignments.\n\n3.2 A shift longer than the Appendix A maximum is an exceedance unless the site manager extended it under section 4.\n\n## 4 Shift extension\n\n4.1 The bleep-holding site manager may extend a shift by up to 02:00 beyond the Appendix A maximum.\n\n4.2 An extension stands only if the shift extension authorisation for that shift is filed and signed by the site manager. An extension without a filed, signed authorisation is treated as no extension.\n\n4.3 A shift longer than the Appendix A maximum plus the extension allowed by 4.1 is an extension exceedance, measured against that extended limit.\n\n## 5 Rest\n\n5.1 The minimum rest before a shift is the length of the preceding duty period, and not less than 11:00.\n\n5.2 Rest runs from the end of the preceding duty period to the start of the next shift. On-call from home does not end a rest period.\n\n## 6 Rolling hours\n\n6.1 Duty periods may not total more than 60:00 in any 7 consecutive days, 110:00 in any 14 consecutive days or 190:00 in any 28 consecutive days.\n\n6.2 Days are calendar days in UK local time, and each duty period counts in full on the day it starts.\n\n## 7 On-call\n\n7.1 On-call served on site counts in full as duty. On-call from home counts as one quarter of its length.\n\n7.2 A nurse called in from on-call at home starts the shift at the time they report, including any transfer; the on-call before the call-in still counts as one quarter.\n\n## 8 Records\n\n8.1 The ward timesheet is the record of clock-in and clock-out times and of the ward assignments worked. The shift-actuals record is a transcription and yields to the ward timesheet.\n\n8.2 Shift extension authorisations are the record of extensions. The authorisation is the scanned form the extension-authorisations register points to; an extension stands only on an authorisation the site manager has signed, and an authorisation is read as it stands in the register when the audit is closed. The extension flag in the shift-actuals record is a transcription.\n\n8.3 The site manager's bleep-log voice notes are the record of call-ins, transfers and where an on-call was served.\n\n## Appendix A: maximum shift (hh:mm)\n\n| Shift start (UK local) | 1-2 ward assignments | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 or more |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| 06:00 to 13:29 | 13:00 | 12:30 | 12:00 | 11:30 | 11:00 |\n| 13:30 to 13:59 | 12:45 | 12:15 | 11:45 | 11:15 | 10:45 |\n| 14:00 to 17:29 | 12:00 | 11:30 | 11:00 | 10:30 | 10:00 |\n| 17:30 to 04:59 | 11:00 | 10:30 | 10:00 | 09:30 | 09:00 |\n| 05:00 to 05:59 | 12:00 | 11:30 | 11:00 | 10:30 | 10:00 |\n\n"}}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_017PUfk8N3W8ttADV1r5kiGb","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}
